title: startup write-sentinel test in SmtpRelayQueue::new catches permission errors early
description: relay_queue.rs SmtpRelayQueue::new writes and removes a .write_test sentinel in both queue_dir and queue_dir/dead before accepting the queue as valid. This is correct defensive design: it surfaces permission errors at startup rather than at first enqueue (which could be hours later under low traffic). The Unix test new_fails_when_queue_dir_is_not_writable covers this. A future contributor might consider removing it as 'unnecessary overhead' — it is not; the early-failure guarantee is worth the two file ops.
